name: useHaptics
summary: Vibration, from simple taps to custom-shaped waveforms.
plain: Makes the phone buzz. Standard patterns cover ordinary taps and confirmations. On this device you can also design your own vibration shape, rising and falling in intensity, which is how you make a distinctive feel rather than a generic buzz.
description: Standard patterns come from expo-haptics. Beyond that, the native module reports the actual vibrator hardware: whether amplitude can be varied, its resonant frequency, and which composition primitives it supports. Android 16 envelope effects are built with BasicEnvelopeBuilder from intensity and sharpness control points and must finish at zero intensity. This Pixel supports them, which is how the thinking ramp and alert pulses are produced.

returns.name: hasAmplitudeControl
returns.desc: Whether vibration strength can be varied rather than just on and off.

returns.name: envelopeSupported
returns.desc: Whether custom envelope waveforms can be played.

returns.name: resonantFrequencyHz
returns.desc: The frequency at which the actuator is most efficient. Around 134 Hz here.

returns.name: supportedPrimitives
returns.desc: Composition building blocks the hardware provides, such as click, tick, thud and rise.

returns.name: source
returns.desc: Where the numbers came from. There is no 'simulated' value: a reading is real, derived from real readings, or unavailable.

actions.name: selection()
actions.desc: Faint tick for moving between options: sliders, wheel pickers, tab changes.
actions.output: Resolves once dispatched. No-op on web; failures are logged rather than thrown.

actions.name: light() / medium() / heavy()
actions.desc: Impact taps of increasing weight, for presses, reveals and destructive confirmations.
actions.output: Resolves once dispatched. No-op on web.

actions.name: success() / warning() / error()
actions.desc: Notification patterns that carry meaning: a double pulse, a buzz, a triple pulse. Use them consistently.
actions.output: Resolves once dispatched. No-op on web.

actions.name: playEnvelope(points, sharpness?)
actions.desc: Plays a custom waveform on Android 16 and later. Check envelopeSupported first.

inputs.name: points
inputs.type: { intensity: number; sharpness: number; durationMs: number }[]
inputs.desc: Steps of the curve; intensity and sharpness are 0 to 1. The envelope must end at intensity 0, which the module appends for you.

actions.output: Returns true when the effect was dispatched, false when envelopes are unsupported or the call failed. It never throws.

actions.name: playPrimitives(steps)
actions.desc: Chains hardware primitives into a composition, Android 11 and later.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.type: { primitive: string; scale?: number; delayMs?: number }[]
inputs.desc: primitive is one of supportedPrimitives; scale sets strength 0 to 1; delayMs is the gap before that step.

actions.output: Returns true when the composition was dispatched, false when the native module is absent or the call failed.

actions.name: cancel()
actions.desc: Stops any vibration immediately, including an envelope or composition in progress.

actions.name: triggerHaptic(type?)
actions.desc: Plays a standard platform pattern. No-op on web.
actions.output: `Promise<void>` — resolves when dispatched; failures are logged, not thrown

agentNote: Attach haptics to every touchable, preferably through HapticButton. Check envelopeSupported before using envelopes and fall back to a standard pattern.
